also_written: John Simmonds (Present column of the 1812 roll)
Corporal John Simmons (family narrative, N. Simmons 1896; Quaife says only a private)
persons.note: On the muster-roll of the company to 31 May 1812 (Quaife 1913, Appendix VIII), enlisted 14 Mar 1810 for five years, to 14 Mar 1815. On the 31 May roll; his widow's captivity is in Woodward's and Helm's lists, and the family narrative (via Quaife) places him at the wagons. After 14 August: Killed defending the baggage wagons; his son David was killed in the children's wagon.

persons.note: Helm's and Woodward's lists of women prisoners. Maiden name only from the 1896 family narrative, which Quaife says "must be used with great caution". After 14 August: Walked with her infant to Green Bay, back via Chicago to Mackinac, then Detroit; reached her parents near Piqua, Ohio, mid-April 1813; died Springville, Iowa, 1857.
